model.name: Document / Record
model.purpose: Give agents one format-neutral vocabulary for treating a document as a governed record: a stable information object whose identity outlives any file, carried through immutable versions and multiple instantiations, made relyable by signatures, timestamps and custody evidence, and disposed of under an authorised retention regime.
model.scope_statement: Covers the record as an aggregate root over its versions, instantiations, signatures, provenance, events, retention assignments, holds and access decisions, from creation or capture through disposition. Excludes the semantics of what the record is about, the agents named in it, the aggregations that hold it, and any particular storage or interface technology.
in_scope: Record identity, designation and official reference numbers
Documentary form/genre and business classification membership
Content structure, components, attachments and significant properties
Immutable version chain, supersession and amendment
Instantiations: renditions, carriers, originals, duplicates, certified copies and extracts
Format identification, rendering environment, fixity and preservation actions
Authorship, approval, ownership, custody and stewardship roles as references
Issuance under mandate and entry into custodial or public registers
Signatures, seals, attestations, trusted timestamps and dated validation outcomes
Provenance, derivation and unbroken chain of custody
Status vocabulary, lifecycle events, audit trail and temporal anchors
Retention classes, disposition authority, holds, disposition execution and surviving evidence
Security marking, access decisions, rights, licensing and personal-data constraints
Metadata alignment, exchange packaging and projections
out_of_scope: Subject-matter semantics of the record's content (contract obligations, clinical findings, financial postings)
Attributes and identity of persons and organizations named as agents
Archival arrangement and description of fonds, series and collections (WM-REC-015)
Identifier scheme registration, syntax and resolution policy (naming model)
Calendar systems, working-day arithmetic and duration algebra (time model)
Message transport, delivery and receipt semantics (communication model)
Byte storage, replication, tiering and infrastructure operations
Workflow and case management beyond record-affecting events
Full-text indexing, retrieval ranking and search relevance
Statutory interpretation of exemptions; the model carries markings, not legal conclusions
Cryptographic key generation and hardware security module operation

boundary_notes.distinction: Aggregation levels, archival arrangement and multi-level description belong to WM-REC-015. RiC separates Record and RecordSet as distinct classes; this model instantiates the Record side and stores only membership references and the aggregate identifier at time of filing.

PROV-O and RiC-O both keep Agent disjoint from the resource. This model stores role-qualified references (author, approver, signatory, custodian) and the basis of the role assertion, never agent attributes.

Scheme governance, syntax and resolution commitments (as in the DOI/ISO 26324 social infrastructure) live in the naming model; this model records scheme, value, assigning authority and granularity only.
Calendar systems and period arithmetic live elsewhere; this model constrains time values to RFC 3339 instants with explicit offset and separates event time from observation time.
eIDAS treats an electronic registered delivery service as a distinct service from an electronic document. A message is a communication act; its attachment resolves to a record governed here.
A dataset governed by a schema is not a record. It becomes a record here only when fixed as an instantiation with fixity, retention and access controls attached.
PREMIS distinguishes File and Bitstream Objects from the Intellectual Entity. One record may span many files and one file may carry many records; storage location is a reference, not identity.

sources.title: ISO 15489-1:2016 Information and documentation — Records management — Part 1: Concepts and principles
sources.relevance: Normative frame for records, metadata for records, records systems, records processes and the characteristics of authoritative records (authenticity, reliability, integrity, usability). Catalogue record only; full text is paywalled and returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch.

sources.title: DCMI Metadata Terms
sources.relevance: Descriptive metadata facet: identifier, title, creator, issued, modified, valid, format, extent, medium, language, type, accessRights, license, provenance, isVersionOf/hasVersion, replaces/isReplacedBy, conformsTo.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Entity/Activity/Agent model plus wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, actedOnBehalfOf, Revision and Bundle — the derivation and responsibility layer of this model.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Mandates an explicit UTC relationship (Z or ±hh:mm) on every timestamp, defines the -00:00 unknown-local-offset convention, leap-second second value 60 and optional fractional seconds.

sources.title: RFC 3161: Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Time-Stamp Protocol (TSP)
sources.relevance: Proof-of-existence token binding a message imprint hash, hash algorithm, TSA-allocated serial number, genTime, accuracy, TSA identity and optional nonce and ordering flag.

sources.title: PREMIS Data Dictionary for Preservation Metadata, Version 3.0
sources.relevance: Intellectual Entity / Representation / File / Bitstream object categories, plus Event, Agent and Rights entities and the fixity, format, significantProperties and storage semantic units. loc.gov returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; content verified through indexed search extracts.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 (eIDAS), Article 3 — Definitions
sources.organization: European Union (text as published by The National Archives, legislation.gov.uk)
sources.relevance: Definitions of electronic document, electronic signature and its advanced/qualified tiers, electronic seal and its tiers, electronic time stamp and its qualified tier, validation, and electronic registered delivery service.

sources.title: International Council on Archives Records in Contexts Ontology (ICA RiC-O) version 1.1
sources.relevance: Record, RecordPart, RecordSet, Instantiation, Agent, Activity, Mandate, Rule, CarrierType, DocumentaryFormType classes and partitive, provenance and instantiation relations; authority for separating record resource from instantiation.

sources.title: Media Types registry
sources.relevance: Normative value space for mediaType on instantiations and exchange packages; eleven top-level types; registration under RFC 6838 with Standards Tree and expert review procedures.

sources.title: C2PA Technical Specification
sources.organization: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
sources.relevance: Manifest, claim, claim signature, assertions, ingredients, hard and soft bindings, manifest store and validation/trust model; requires X.509 signing and recommends RFC 3161 time-stamping, with manifests expiring on credential revocation when untimestamped.

sources.title: Universal Electronic Records Management (ERM) Requirements
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration
sources.relevance: Lifecycle requirement grouping used to shape the operating surface: Capture, Maintenance and Use, Disposal, Transfer, Metadata and Reporting.

sources.title: Metadata guidance tables for transfer of permanent electronic records (case file appendix)
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration
sources.relevance: Concrete mandatory element set for embedded case files: Identifier:FileName, MessageDigest, Title, CreationDate, ModifiedDate, AccessRestrictions — evidence that digest and restriction status are transfer-critical.

sources.title: UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Commerce (1996) with additional article 5 bis (1998)
sources.organization: United Nations Commission on International Trade Law
sources.relevance: Functional-equivalence doctrine: criteria under which electronic communications satisfy paper concepts of writing, signature and original — the legal basis for treating an instantiation as an original of record.

sources.title: PRONOM technical registry
sources.relevance: Registry of file formats, software products and technical components used for preservation, with DROID-based automatic identification; source of format identifiers finer-grained than media types.

sources.title: What is a DOI? (DOI system and ISO 26324)
sources.relevance: Model of a governed global identifier: prefix/suffix syntax, Handle-based resolution, and persistence resting on organizational commitment rather than technology — the second tier of the identity priority.

sources.title: MoReq2010: Modular Requirements for Records Systems, Volume 1 — Core Services & Plug-in Modules
sources.relevance: Core-service decomposition of a records system, including classification, records, metadata, disposal scheduling and disposal holding services, system-assigned entity identifiers and mandatory event history. Retrieved as PDF; content verified through indexed search extracts rather than direct text parsing.

bundles.name: Identity, documentary form and classification
bundles.description: What the record is, how it is named and referenced, what documentary genre it belongs to, and where it sits in a business classification scheme and archival aggregation.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 treats classification and identification as the controls from which every later recordkeeping decision derives, and RiC-O separates the record from the sets that contain it; an agent cannot apply retention, access or authenticity rules before these are fixed.

layers.name: Identity and designation
layers.description: The stable identifier of the record as an information object and the human-facing titles and reference numbers layered on top of it.

findings.name: Record identity anchor
findings.description: The identifier that denotes the record independently of any file, version or rendition, its scheme, its granularity and its non-reuse guarantee.

questions.text: Which system is the authoritative master for this record's identifier and from which registered scheme is the value drawn?
Does the identifier denote the record, one version, or one instantiation?
What guarantees that the identifier is never reused after disposition or system migration?
Which legacy or alternate identifiers exist and on what basis are they asserted equivalent?

data_elements.name: recordIdentifier
data_elements.description: Primary identifier of the record, chosen by the identity priority rule.

data_elements.name: identifierScheme
data_elements.description: Registered scheme that governs the identifier's syntax and resolution.

data_elements.name: identifierGranularity
data_elements.description: Whether the identifier denotes the record, a version or an instantiation.

data_elements.name: alternateIdentifier
data_elements.description: Legacy or parallel identifiers with scheme and equivalence basis.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identifier values are inline reference data that must appear in every projection, including existence-level ones. The evidencing artifact for identifier assignment is the register entry produced under issuance and registration, so a separate artifact here would duplicate it.

findings.name: Designation and reference numbers
findings.description: Titles, alternative and translated titles, and the official reference numbers quoted on the face of the record, kept strictly distinct from identity.

questions.text: What is the official title of the record, in which language and script is it recorded, and who set it?
Which reference numbers appear on the face of the record and which authority allocated each?
How are superseded or translated titles retained without ever being treated as identifiers?

data_elements.name: title
data_elements.description: Official name given to the record.

data_elements.name: alternativeTitle
data_elements.description: Translated, short or superseded titles with their validity periods.

data_elements.name: titleLanguage
data_elements.description: Language of the recorded title.

data_elements.name: faceReferenceNumber
data_elements.description: Reference numbers printed or displayed on the record itself.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Designation is descriptive inline metadata carried on the record; no separate artifact is produced by titling, and treating a title list as an artifact would invite its use as an identifier, which the identity rule forbids.

layers.name: Documentary form and classification
layers.description: The genre of the record and its placement in a business classification scheme and archival aggregation, which drive the rules that later apply to it.

findings.name: Documentary form and genre
findings.description: The documentary form the record takes (contract, certificate, invoice, minutes, licence) typed against a controlled vocabulary, and the rules that follow from that form.

questions.text: What documentary form does this record take and from which controlled vocabulary is the term drawn?
Which obligations, signature requirements or retention consequences follow automatically from that form?
Can one record carry more than one documentary form, such as a certificate inside a covering letter?
Who approves additions to the form vocabulary and how are retired terms handled?

data_elements.name: documentaryForm
data_elements.description: Controlled term for the record's genre.

data_elements.name: formVocabulary
data_elements.description: Reference to the vocabulary and version supplying the term.

data_elements.name: resourceType
data_elements.description: Coarse resource type aligned to DCMI Type for cross-domain exchange.

data_elements.name: secondaryForm
data_elements.description: Additional forms carried by components of a compound record.

artifacts.name: Documentary form vocabulary
artifacts.description: The governed term list of documentary forms, with notations, definitions, deprecations and the rules each form triggers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Scheme IRI plus version tag; individual terms identified by scheme-scoped notation, never by display label.

findings.name: Business classification and aggregation membership
findings.description: Filing of the record under a classification class and its membership in aggregations, with the boundary to the archival aggregation model held explicitly.

questions.text: Under which classification class is the record filed and which version of the scheme was in force at filing?
Which aggregations does the record belong to and is membership exclusive?
When the scheme is reorganised, is the historic class retained alongside the new one?
If more than one class applies, which one determines retention and access?

data_elements.name: classificationClass
data_elements.description: Notation of the class under which the record is filed.

data_elements.name: classificationSchemeVersion
data_elements.description: Version of the classification scheme in force at filing.

data_elements.name: aggregationMembership
data_elements.description: References to the file, series, case or fonds containing the record.

data_elements.name: classificationEffectiveFrom
data_elements.description: Instant from which the class assignment applies.

artifacts.name: Business classification scheme (file plan)
artifacts.description: The hierarchical scheme of classes under which records are filed, with effective dates, retention linkage and superseded versions retained.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Scheme identifier issued by the owning organisation plus effective-from date; superseded versions kept and never overwritten.

bundles.name: Content, versions and manifestations
bundles.description: What the record says, the immutable states its content passes through, and the format-specific and carrier-specific realisations that make it readable.
bundles.rationale: PREMIS distinguishes Intellectual Entity, Representation, File and Bitstream, and RiC-O separates record resource from instantiation; collapsing these layers makes format migration indistinguishable from content change and destroys the evidentiary chain.

layers.name: Content and components
layers.description: The body of the record, its structural parts, attachments and the properties that must survive any transformation.

findings.name: Content structure, components and completeness
findings.description: Which parts make up the complete record, which are essential to its meaning, and how completeness is verified at capture.

questions.text: Which components make up the complete record and which of them are essential rather than incidental?
Which significant properties must be preserved for the record to remain usable and understandable?
In which languages is the content expressed and which language version is authoritative for interpretation?
How is completeness verified before the record is declared captured?

data_elements.name: component
data_elements.description: An addressable part of the record: body, annex, attachment or embedded object, with its role.

data_elements.name: significantProperties
data_elements.description: Characteristics that must survive migration or rendition for the record to remain usable.

data_elements.name: contentLanguage
data_elements.description: Languages in which the content is expressed.

data_elements.name: extent
data_elements.description: Size or duration of the content, such as page count, word count or playing time.

artifacts.name: Record component manifest
artifacts.description: Itemised inventory of the components constituting one version of the record, with roles, order, essentiality and per-component digests.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Record identifier plus version identifier; exactly one manifest per version, regenerated only by issuing a new version.

layers.name: Versions and instantiations
layers.description: The immutable version chain of content states and the multiple physical or digital instantiations that realise each state.

findings.name: Version chain and immutability
findings.description: How a content state is fixed, how versions supersede and amend one another, and the prohibition on editing an issued version in place.

questions.text: Which event fixes a version and makes it immutable, and who is competent to trigger it?
Which version is currently authoritative and which versions does it supersede or amend?
How are drafts distinguished from issued versions for retention and access purposes?
What reason, authority and change description are recorded for each new version?

data_elements.name: versionIdentifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of one immutable content state.

data_elements.name: versionSequence
data_elements.description: Monotonic sequence number of the version within the record.

data_elements.name: versionState
data_elements.description: Whether the version is draft, issued, superseded or withdrawn.

data_elements.name: supersedes
data_elements.description: Reference to the version or record this one replaces.

data_elements.name: changeNote
data_elements.description: Statement of what changed and why.

artifacts.name: Version history
artifacts.description: Append-only chain of version entries with sequence, fixing event, issuing agent, change note and supersession links.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Record identifier plus zero-padded monotonic version sequence; sequences are never reused or renumbered.

findings.name: Instantiation, copy and original status
findings.description: Format-specific and carrier-specific realisations of a version, and the legal distinction between the original of record, duplicates, certified copies and extracts.

questions.text: Which instantiation is the original of record and where is it held?
Is a given instantiation a faithful rendition, a derivative, a certified copy or an extract, and who attests it?
What criteria make a digitised surrogate acceptable in place of an analogue original?
How are two instantiations of the same version proven to carry the same content?

data_elements.name: instantiationIdentifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of one realisation of a version on a carrier or in a format.

data_elements.name: instantiationRole
data_elements.description: Original of record, duplicate, certified copy, extract, rendition or preservation master.

data_elements.name: carrierType
data_elements.description: Physical or digital carrier on which the instantiation exists.

data_elements.name: storageLocation
data_elements.description: Reference to where the instantiation is held, resolved by the storage model.

artifacts.name: Certified copy or extract attestation
artifacts.description: Statement by a competent authority that a named instantiation is a true copy or a faithful extract of a named source, with the scope of what was omitted.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Attestation number allocated by the certifying authority plus RFC 3339 issue instant; the attestation references both source and copy identifiers.

layers.name: Format, fixity and preservation
layers.description: Technical identification of instantiations, the environment needed to render them, and the integrity and preservation controls applied over time.

findings.name: Format identification and rendering environment
findings.description: How each instantiation's format is identified against registries and what software and hardware environment is required to render it.

questions.text: Which registered media type and which format-registry identifier apply to this instantiation?
answer_data: media type from the IANA registry
format registry identifier such as a PRONOM PUID

questions.text: How was the format determined — declared by the producer or identified by a tool?
What environment is required to render the instantiation faithfully?
What is the obsolescence risk for this format and what migration or emulation path is planned?

data_elements.name: mediaType
data_elements.description: IANA-registered media type of the instantiation.

data_elements.name: formatRegistryIdentifier
data_elements.description: Fine-grained format identifier from a technical registry, such as a PRONOM PUID.

data_elements.name: environmentDependency
data_elements.description: Software, hardware or resource dependencies needed to render the instantiation.

data_elements.name: byteSize
data_elements.description: Size of the instantiation in bytes.

artifacts.name: Format characterisation report
artifacts.description: Tool-produced technical description of an instantiation: identified format, version, validity, well-formedness, extracted properties and dependencies.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Instantiation identifier plus tool identifier, tool version and RFC 3339 run instant; reports are additive and earlier reports are retained.

findings.name: Fixity and preservation actions
findings.description: Baseline digests, verification history, declared preservation level and the actions applied to keep instantiations readable, including those that change bytes.

questions.text: Which algorithm and digest value were recorded at capture, and by which agent?
When was fixity last verified, at what frequency, and what was the outcome?
Which preservation actions have been applied and did any of them change the bytes?
What happens when a fixity check fails, and who is notified?

data_elements.name: fixityAlgorithm
data_elements.description: Named digest algorithm used; multiple algorithms may be recorded for agility.

data_elements.name: fixityValue
data_elements.description: Digest value bound to a specific instantiation and algorithm.

data_elements.name: fixityComputedAt
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the digest was computed.

data_elements.name: preservationLevel
data_elements.description: Declared level of preservation commitment and replication for the instantiation.

data_elements.name: preservationEvent
data_elements.description: References to normalisation, migration, repair or replication events.

artifacts.name: Fixity manifest
artifacts.description: Set of digests covering the instantiations and artifacts of a record or package, with algorithms, computation instants and the computing agent.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Record or package identifier plus algorithm set plus RFC 3339 computation instant; manifests accumulate and are never overwritten.

bundles.name: Agency, authority and issuance
bundles.description: Who is responsible for the record, who owns and who keeps it, and the act of issuing it under a mandate and entering it into a register.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 makes assigned responsibility a precondition of trustworthy recordkeeping, RiC-O models Mandate and Agent as distinct contextual entities, and eIDAS makes the issuing legal person material to legal effect; ownership must be separable from custody.

layers.name: Agents, ownership and custody
layers.description: Role-qualified references to the agents who made, approved, own and keep the record.

findings.name: Authorship and responsibility roles
findings.description: Who authored, contributed to, approved and was addressed by the record, expressed as role-qualified references rather than embedded agent descriptions.

questions.text: Which agent is the author of record and which agents merely contributed?
Who approved or authorised issue, and under what delegation of authority?
Who are the intended addressees or recipients, and does that constrain access?
How is a role recorded when the responsible agent cannot be identified?

data_elements.name: author
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent responsible for making the record.

data_elements.name: approver
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent who authorised issue.

data_elements.name: addressee
data_elements.description: Reference to the intended recipient of the record.

data_elements.name: roleAssertionBasis
data_elements.description: Evidence on which a responsibility role is asserted.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Agent attributes are governed by the person and organization models; this finding stores only role-qualified references, and the artifacts that evidence responsibility are the signature object and the event history recorded in other findings.

findings.name: Ownership, custody and stewardship
findings.description: The separation between the record owner and the custodian or registrar acting on the owner's behalf, and the terms limiting custodial power.

questions.text: Who owns the record and who currently has custody of it?
What may the custodian not do — can they widen access, migrate formats or dispose?
How and when does ownership itself transfer, and what evidence is required?

data_elements.name: recordOwner
data_elements.description: Reference to the author or issuing organization accountable for the record.

data_elements.name: custodian
data_elements.description: Reference to the party currently holding the record on the owner's behalf.

data_elements.name: custodyTerms
data_elements.description: Reference to the agreement or policy defining custodial powers and limits.

data_elements.name: ownershipTransferEvent
data_elements.description: Events at which ownership, as distinct from custody, changed hands.

artifacts.name: Custody or deposit agreement
artifacts.description: Instrument setting out what the custodian may and may not do with the record, the service levels and the conditions for return or transfer.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Agreement reference allocated by the owning party plus version; superseded versions retained for the period they governed.

layers.name: Issuance and registration
layers.description: The act of issuing the record under a mandate in a jurisdiction, and its entry into a custodial or public register.

findings.name: Issuance, mandate and register entry
findings.description: The legal basis and jurisdiction under which the record was issued, and the register entry that anchors it in a custodial system.

questions.text: Under which mandate, statute or delegated authority was the record issued?
In which jurisdiction and at which place was it issued, and does that determine the applicable rules?
Is the record registered, in which register, under what entry number, and at what instant?
Is the register public, and what is disclosed at existence level when content is withheld?

data_elements.name: issuingAuthority
data_elements.description: Reference to the legal person that issued the record.

data_elements.name: mandate
data_elements.description: Reference to the instrument authorising issue.

data_elements.name: jurisdiction
data_elements.description: Legal jurisdiction governing the record.

data_elements.name: registerEntryNumber
data_elements.description: Entry number allocated by the register authority.

data_elements.name: registeredAt
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant of registration.

artifacts.name: Register entry or registration certificate
artifacts.description: The custodial or public register line that anchors the record, with entry number, registering authority, registration instant and the existence-level fields disclosed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Register identifier plus entry number allocated by the register authority; entry numbers are monotonic per register and never reused.

bundles.name: Authenticity and evidentiary value
bundles.description: Why the record can be relied on: signatures and seals bound to fixed content, trusted timestamps, dated validation outcomes, derivation provenance and an unbroken chain of custody.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 makes authenticity and integrity defining characteristics of an authoritative record, eIDAS attaches legal effect to signature and timestamp tiers, and PROV-O and C2PA supply the derivation and binding structures; validity is time-dependent and must be recorded as evidence, not asserted as a flag.

layers.name: Signatures, seals and validation evidence
layers.description: Signature and seal objects bound to specific content, the timestamps that fix their moment, and the dated results of validating them.

findings.name: Signature, seal and attestation
findings.description: Signatures, seals and attestations applied to a version or instantiation, their assurance tier, their signatory and exactly what content each binds.

questions.text: What signature or seal type was applied and at which assurance tier?
answer_data: assurance tier such as simple, advanced or qualified

questions.text: Which exact content does each signature bind — a version, an instantiation, or a byte range?
Who is the signatory or sealing legal person, and on which certificate or credential does the signature rest?
What must hold for the signature to have legal effect in the governing jurisdiction?
answer_data: required tier for the record type

data_elements.name: signatureIdentifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the signature, seal or attestation object.

data_elements.name: signatureType
data_elements.description: Handwritten, electronic signature, advanced or qualified signature, electronic seal, or other attestation.

data_elements.name: signedContentBinding
data_elements.description: Reference and digest of the exact content the signature binds.

data_elements.name: claimedSigningTime
data_elements.description: Signing time asserted by the signatory, distinct from any trusted timestamp.

data_elements.name: signingCertificate
data_elements.description: Reference to the certificate or credential used.

artifacts.name: Signature, seal or attestation object
artifacts.description: The signature itself — detached or embedded — carrying the bound digest, the signing credential chain and the claimed signing time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Signature identifier plus the digest of the content it binds; a signature is never re-pointed to different content.

findings.name: Timestamping and validation evidence
findings.description: Trusted time-stamp tokens proving existence at a time, validation outcomes recorded with their own validation instant and policy, and the renewal of evidence before algorithms weaken.

questions.text: Is there a trusted time-stamp token binding the content to a time, and which authority issued it?
What was the validation outcome, at which validation instant, and under which validation policy?
How is the evidence renewed before its algorithms or certificates weaken?
Which provenance manifest, if any, travels with the rendered asset, and does it survive rendition?

data_elements.name: timeStampToken
data_elements.description: Reference to the trusted token binding a digest to a time.

data_elements.name: timeStampGenTime
data_elements.description: Generation time asserted by the timestamping authority.

data_elements.name: validationOutcome
data_elements.description: Result of validating a signature, seal or manifest at a specific moment.

data_elements.name: validatedAt
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which validation was performed.

data_elements.name: validationPolicy
data_elements.description: Reference to the policy under which validation was performed.

artifacts.name: Trusted time-stamp token
artifacts.description: Proof-of-existence token binding a message imprint hash, algorithm, authority-allocated serial number and generation time with stated accuracy.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Timestamping authority identity plus the serial number it allocated; serials are unique per authority.

artifacts.name: Signature validation report
artifacts.description: Dated statement of the outcome of validating a signature, seal or provenance manifest, naming the policy, trust anchors and revocation data used.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Subject signature identifier plus RFC 3339 validation instant plus policy identifier; reports accumulate and earlier outcomes are never overwritten.

layers.name: Provenance and chain of custody
layers.description: Where the record came from and who held it at every moment between creation and now.

findings.name: Derivation and provenance graph
findings.description: The activities that generated the record, the sources it derives from, and the agents associated with each generating activity.

questions.text: Which activity generated this record or version, and when did it start and end?
Which prior records was it derived from, and is the derivation a revision, an extract or a quotation?
Which agent was associated with each generating activity, and on whose behalf did they act?
Where a machine or model produced content, what tool, version and parameters are recorded?

data_elements.name: generatingActivity
data_elements.description: Reference to the activity that produced the record or version.

data_elements.name: derivedFrom
data_elements.description: References to source entities from which this record was derived.

data_elements.name: derivationType
data_elements.description: Revision, extract, quotation, translation, redaction or format migration.

data_elements.name: generatedAt
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which generation completed.

artifacts.name: Provenance bundle or content credential manifest
artifacts.description: A named set of provenance descriptions covering entities, activities, agents and derivations, or an asset-embedded manifest with assertions, ingredients and bindings.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bundle identifier for provenance sets; asset-embedded manifests are identified by their claim signature and the hard binding they assert.

findings.name: Chain of custody and hand-over
findings.description: The gapless sequence of custody intervals, hand-over receipts and integrity checks that allows the record to be relied on as evidence.

questions.text: Who held the record over each interval and are there any unexplained gaps?
What receipt or acknowledgement evidences each hand-over?
Was integrity verified at dispatch and again at receipt, and by whom?
How is the chain kept intact when a system migration rewrites storage or re-encodes content?

data_elements.name: custodyEvent
data_elements.description: An event at which responsibility for holding the record changed.

data_elements.name: custodyFrom
data_elements.description: Party relinquishing custody.

data_elements.name: custodyTo
data_elements.description: Party receiving custody.

data_elements.name: custodyChangedAt
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant of the custody change.

artifacts.name: Custody transfer receipt
artifacts.description: Signed acknowledgement of hand-over naming both parties, the records covered, the integrity proof presented and the instant custody changed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Transfer reference plus RFC 3339 hand-over instant; both parties retain matching copies bound to the same reference.

bundles.name: State, time and recordkeeping control
bundles.description: The status the record is in, the events that moved it there, the time anchors it carries, and the retention, hold and disposition regime that decides its end.
bundles.rationale: NARA's universal requirements organise records systems by lifecycle from capture through disposal and transfer, MoReq2010 requires an event history on every entity and separates disposal scheduling from disposal holding, and RFC 3339 makes explicit offsets mandatory; state, time and disposition are one control problem.

layers.name: Status, lifecycle events and time
layers.description: Controlled status values, the append-only history of what happened, and the distinct time anchors the record carries.

findings.name: Record status and permitted transitions
findings.description: The controlled status vocabulary, which transitions are permitted from each state, who may authorise them, and how withdrawal differs from destruction.

questions.text: What is the record's current status and since which instant has it held that status?
Which transitions are permitted from the current status and who may authorise each?
Is withdrawal or revocation distinct from destruction, and does a revoked record remain discoverable?

data_elements.name: recordStatus
data_elements.description: Current controlled status: draft, issued, effective, superseded, withdrawn, revoked, transferred or destroyed.

data_elements.name: statusSince
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the current status took effect.

data_elements.name: transitionAuthority
data_elements.description: Role or instrument authorising the transition into the current status.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Status is inline state carried directly on the record and required in every projection including existence-level views; its evidence is the event history artifact in the adjacent finding, so a duplicate artifact would be a second source of truth.

findings.name: Lifecycle events and audit trail
findings.description: The append-only history of everything done to and with the record, using controlled event types with actor, outcome, event time and separately recorded observation time.

questions.text: Which event types are recorded and from which controlled vocabulary are they drawn?
Who performed each event, with what outcome and what detail?
Is the trail append-only and how is its own integrity protected against tampering?
How long is the audit trail retained relative to the record, and does disposition erase it?

data_elements.name: eventIdentifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a single event entry.

data_elements.name: eventType
data_elements.description: Controlled type of the event, such as capture, migration, signing, hold or disposal.

data_elements.name: eventDateTime
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the event occurred.

data_elements.name: eventRecordedAt
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the system learned of and recorded the event.

data_elements.name: eventOutcome
data_elements.description: Outcome code and detail for the event.

artifacts.name: Event history and audit trail
artifacts.description: Append-only sequence of event entries covering every action on the record, each with type, agent, outcome, event time and recording time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Event identifier per entry, ordered by monotonic sequence within the record; entries are never edited, only superseded by correcting entries that cite the original.

findings.name: Temporal anchors and validity periods
findings.description: The distinct time anchors a record carries — created, issued, effective, expiry, received, observed — their precision, and the rule separating event time from ingestion time.

questions.text: Which datetime is the legally or operationally decisive one for this record type?
Over what period is the record valid or effective, and may the period be open-ended?
How are event time and observation or ingestion time kept distinct in every record of time?
How are dates of unknown precision or unknown local offset recorded?

data_elements.name: createdAt
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant of creation of the content.

data_elements.name: issuedAt
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant of formal issuance.

data_elements.name: effectiveFrom
data_elements.description: Start of the period over which the record is valid or in force.

data_elements.name: effectiveTo
data_elements.description: End of the validity period, absent when open-ended.

data_elements.name: receivedAt
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the record was received or captured by the keeping system.

data_elements.name: temporalPrecision
data_elements.description: Declared precision of a recorded time value where it is not instant-level.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Time anchors are inline scalar values attached to the record, its versions and its events; the artifacts that carry temporal evidence are the trusted time-stamp token and the event history, both defined in other findings.

layers.name: Retention, disposition and holds
layers.description: The authorised schedule that decides the record's fate, the suspensions that override it, and the evidence that survives execution.

findings.name: Retention class and disposition authority
findings.description: The retention class assigned to the record, the instrument authorising it, the trigger that starts the clock and the action due at the end.

questions.text: Which retention class applies and under which authority instrument and citation?
What event triggers the retention clock and how is that trigger detected?
Is the record permanent or temporary, and what disposition action falls due at the end of the period?
When two schedules apply to the same record, which one prevails?

data_elements.name: retentionClass
data_elements.description: Class assigning the record to a retention regime.

data_elements.name: dispositionAuthorityCitation
data_elements.description: Citation of the instrument authorising the retention and disposition of the class.

data_elements.name: retentionTriggerEvent
data_elements.description: Event type that starts the retention period.

data_elements.name: retentionPeriod
data_elements.description: Duration for which the record must be kept after the trigger.

data_elements.name: dispositionDueAt
data_elements.description: Computed date at which the disposition action becomes due.

artifacts.name: Retention schedule or disposition authority instrument
artifacts.description: The authorised schedule mapping classes to trigger events, periods, permanence and disposition actions, with its jurisdiction and period of force.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authority citation allocated by the competent archival or regulatory authority plus item number and version; superseded schedules are retained for records disposed of under them.

findings.name: Holds and disposition suspension
findings.description: Legal holds and other suspensions that override retention schedules until explicitly released, and the mechanism that prevents automated disposal of held records.

questions.text: What is the scope of the hold — this record, its aggregation, or a query-defined set resolved at a moment in time?
answer_data: resolved record set with resolution instant

questions.text: Who placed the hold, under what proceeding or authority, and when?
What must be true before the hold can be released and disposition resumed?
How is hold state surfaced so that no automated process can dispose of a held record?
answer_data: hold check in the disposition function
failure mode if the check is unavailable

data_elements.name: holdIdentifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the hold instrument.

data_elements.name: holdBasis
data_elements.description: Proceeding, investigation or statutory basis for the hold.

data_elements.name: holdPlacedAt
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the hold took effect.

data_elements.name: holdReleasedAt
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant of release, absent while the hold is active.

data_elements.name: holdActive
data_elements.description: Whether any hold currently suspends disposition of this record.

artifacts.name: Legal hold notice
artifacts.description: Instrument placing or releasing a hold, naming the scope, the basis, the issuing authority and the instants of placement and release.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Hold identifier plus issuing authority reference; release is a new dated entry against the same hold identifier, never a deletion.

findings.name: Disposition execution and surviving evidence
findings.description: Carrying out destruction, transfer or permanent retention, and the evidence and tombstone that outlive the record itself.

questions.text: Who authorised the disposition and was the absence of any hold verified at that moment?
What method was used and is it verifiable as irreversible for the carrier concerned?
What evidence survives destruction and which metadata fields are kept as a tombstone?
For transfer, what accession identifier and integrity proof did the receiving body return?

data_elements.name: dispositionExecutedAt
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the disposition action was carried out.

data_elements.name: dispositionMethod
data_elements.description: Method of destruction, transfer or permanent retention applied.

data_elements.name: tombstoneFields
data_elements.description: Minimal metadata retained after the record body is gone.

data_elements.name: accessionReference
data_elements.description: Identifier allocated by the receiving archives on transfer.

artifacts.name: Disposition certificate
artifacts.description: Signed evidence that a named set of records was destroyed under a named authority, listing identifiers, method, authorisers and the execution instant.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Disposition run identifier plus record identifier; retained under its own schedule after the record itself no longer exists.

artifacts.name: Transfer and accession manifest
artifacts.description: Inventory of records transferred to another custodian or to permanent archives, with digests, counts, transfer instant and the accession returned.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Accession number allocated by the receiving archives plus the sending party's transfer identifier; both are retained on each side.

bundles.name: Access, rights and interoperability
bundles.description: Who may see what, on what legal footing content may be reused, and how the record and its evidence move between systems without losing meaning.
bundles.rationale: NARA's transfer guidance makes access restriction status a mandatory transfer element, DCMI supplies accessRights, license and rightsHolder, and IANA and format registries govern the value space for exchange; access and interoperability are governed together because every projection is an access decision.

layers.name: Access, security marking and rights
layers.description: Markings and decisions controlling who may read the record, and the intellectual-property and personal-data constraints on reuse.

findings.name: Access conditions and security marking
findings.description: The security marking and access restriction status carried by the record, the statutory regime behind them, and the recorded decisions on individual requests.

questions.text: What security marking and access restriction status does the record carry, and who set them?
Which statutory access or exemption regime applies, and for how long does the restriction run?
What is disclosed at existence level when the content itself is withheld?
How are grants, denials and emergency access events recorded and reviewed?

data_elements.name: securityMarking
data_elements.description: Confidentiality or protective marking applied to the record.

data_elements.name: accessRestrictionStatus
data_elements.description: Whether access is unrestricted, restricted or closed, and on what basis.

data_elements.name: restrictionBasis
data_elements.description: Statutory or contractual basis for the restriction.

data_elements.name: restrictionReviewDate
data_elements.description: Date on which the restriction must be reviewed or lapses.

artifacts.name: Access decision record
artifacts.description: Entry recording one access request: requester, purpose, requested scope, decision, decision-maker, reasons and the RFC 3339 decision instant.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Request identifier plus RFC 3339 decision instant; denials and break-glass events are recorded with the same fidelity as grants.

findings.name: Rights, licensing and personal data
findings.description: Who holds rights in the content, under what licence it may be reused, and what personal data within it constrains processing and release.

questions.text: Who holds rights in the content and under which licence may it be reused?
Does the record contain personal or special-category data, and on what lawful basis is it processed?
What redactions produced the releasable derivative, and is the unredacted source preserved intact?
answer_data: redaction scope and basis per passage

data_elements.name: rightsHolder
data_elements.description: Reference to the person or organization owning or managing rights in the content.

data_elements.name: license
data_elements.description: Licence granting permission to use the content.

data_elements.name: personalDataCategory
data_elements.description: Categories of personal data present in the record.

data_elements.name: redactionReference
data_elements.description: Reference linking a redacted derivative to its source and to the basis for each redaction.

artifacts.name: Rights statement or licence instrument
artifacts.description: Statement of rights held and the terms under which the content may be reused, redistributed or published.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Licence IRI where a published licence is used; otherwise the instrument reference of the granting party plus version.

artifacts.name: Redaction and release log
artifacts.description: Record of every redaction applied to produce a releasable derivative, with the passage affected, the basis and the approving agent.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derivative instantiation identifier plus source instantiation identifier plus release instant; the derivative is a new instantiation and never overwrites the source.

layers.name: Interoperability and exchange
layers.description: Declared mappings to external metadata standards and the packaging and projection rules for moving records between systems.

findings.name: Metadata alignment and conformance evidence
findings.description: Which external standards the record's metadata is mapped to, where mappings lose information, and what evidence is required before any conformance claim is made.

questions.text: Which external standards is this metadata mapped to, and at which version of each?
Where does a mapping lose information or contradict another target, and how is the loss recorded?
What evidence supports any conformance claim, and who validated it?

data_elements.name: mappingTarget
data_elements.description: External standard to which the metadata is mapped.

data_elements.name: mappingTargetVersion
data_elements.description: Version of the target standard covered by the mapping.

data_elements.name: mappingLossiness
data_elements.description: Statement of what the mapping cannot carry.

data_elements.name: conformanceClaim
data_elements.description: Any asserted conformance, permitted only with a cited evidence artifact.

artifacts.name: Metadata crosswalk specification
artifacts.description: Element-by-element mapping between this model and a named external standard version, marking lossy and unmappable elements.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Mapping identifier plus source and target standard versions; a new target version requires a new mapping, not an edit.

findings.name: Exchange packaging and projections
findings.description: How a record and its evidence are packaged for transfer or publication, and how each projection deliberately omits parts without breaking reconstructability.

questions.text: What package structure and manifest are used, and how is package integrity proven on arrival?
Which projection is being served and which fields does it deliberately omit?
How does a receiving system reconstruct identity, version chain, fixity and events from the package alone?
Which media types, character encodings and normalisation rules apply to the payload?

data_elements.name: packageIdentifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the exchange package.

data_elements.name: packageProfile
data_elements.description: Named packaging profile governing structure and required elements.

data_elements.name: packageFixity
data_elements.description: Digest covering the package as a whole.

data_elements.name: projectionName
data_elements.description: Named subset served to a consumer, such as an existence-level listing, an evidentiary view or a disposition worklist.

artifacts.name: Exchange package manifest
artifacts.description: Self-describing inventory of a submission, archival or dissemination package, listing records, versions, instantiations, digests, events and the profile in force.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Package identifier plus the package-level digest; a re-generated package is a new package with a new identifier.

functions.name: Assign record identity
functions.description: Select and bind the identifier that will denote the record for its whole life, following the identity priority.
preconditions: identity priority evaluated in order and the chosen tier recorded
scheme is registered and its resolution commitment is known
effects: record becomes referenceable across projections
identifier is reserved permanently and never reused, including after disposition

functions.name: Capture or create record
functions.description: Bring an authored or received information object under recordkeeping control.
preconditions: identifier assigned
documentary form and classification selected
access restriction status determined
effects: received bytes preserved unaltered as the capture instantiation
any normalisation recorded as a separate derivative with its own provenance

functions.name: Issue version
functions.description: Fix a new immutable content state and link it into the version chain.
preconditions: issuer authorised for the record's class
prior version exists and is not blocked by a hold that forbids amendment
effects: prior version marked superseded and retained
version sequence incremented and never renumbered

functions.name: Produce instantiation
functions.description: Create a format-specific or carrier-specific realisation of an existing version.
preconditions: source version is fixed
target format identifiable in a media type and format registry
effects: instantiation bound to exactly one version
significant properties compared before and after and any loss recorded

functions.name: Verify fixity
functions.description: Recompute and compare digests for an instantiation or package against its baseline.
preconditions: a baseline fixity value with a named algorithm exists
effects: mismatches raise an integrity incident and trigger recovery from a verified replica
failures are never silently repaired or overwritten

functions.name: Apply signature or seal
functions.description: Bind a signature, seal or attestation to fixed content at a declared assurance tier.
preconditions: content is fixed and its digest computed
credential valid at signing time and of the tier required for the documentary form
effects: signature binds a named digest; any later content change invalidates it rather than migrating with it

functions.name: Timestamp and validate evidence
functions.description: Obtain a trusted time-stamp token and record a dated validation outcome for a signature or manifest.
preconditions: digest algorithm accepted by the validation policy
trust anchors and revocation sources reachable
effects: validity recorded as a dated outcome under a named policy, never as a permanent flag
renewal scheduled ahead of algorithm or certificate weakening

functions.name: Record custody transfer
functions.description: Move holding responsibility to another party without breaking the chain of custody.
preconditions: receiving party accepts the custody terms
fixity verified before dispatch
effects: custody intervals remain gapless
integrity re-verified on receipt and the result recorded on both sides

functions.name: Assign retention
functions.description: Bind the record to a retention class under a named authority and compute when disposition falls due.
preconditions: authority instrument in force for the jurisdiction
trigger event type detectable by the system
effects: disposition becomes schedulable
schedule conflicts resolved by the declared precedence rule and the resolution recorded

functions.name: Place or release hold
functions.description: Suspend or resume disposition for a defined scope of records.
preconditions: scope resolvable at the moment of placement and the resolution instant recorded
effects: disposition blocked for every in-scope record until an explicit, separately authorised release
release recorded as a new dated entry rather than by deleting the hold

functions.name: Execute disposition
functions.description: Carry out destruction, transfer or permanent retention for records whose period has elapsed.
preconditions: retention period elapsed
no active hold at the moment of execution
authority instrument still in force
effects: action is irreversible
evidence artifact and tombstone survive the record and are retained under their own schedule

functions.name: Issue certified copy or extract
functions.description: Produce an attested copy or extract traceable to a named source version.
preconditions: source integrity verified immediately before copying
certifier competent in the governing jurisdiction
effects: copy is marked as a copy and never becomes the original of record
omissions in an extract are stated explicitly in the attestation

functions.name: Evaluate access request
functions.description: Decide and record whether a requester may read a record or a projection of it.
outputs: released projection or refusal with reasons
preconditions: security marking and access restriction status known
statutory regime and exemptions identified
effects: decision, denial or emergency access logged with the decision instant
break-glass access notifies the owner within the declared window

functions.name: Export exchange package
functions.description: Assemble a self-describing package of records and their evidence for transfer or publication.
preconditions: all referenced instantiations resolvable
fixity current for every included instantiation
effects: receiver can reconstruct identity, version chain, fixity and event history from the package alone
omitted fields are declared in the manifest rather than silently dropped

composition.purpose: Records governed here are the members that archival aggregations contain; membership references are stored here, arrangement and multi-level description there.
Authors, approvers, signatories and custodial officers are agents held disjoint from the resource in both PROV-O and RiC-O; only role-qualified references are stored here.
Issuing organizations, custodians, registers and receiving archives are corporate bodies governed elsewhere; eIDAS attaches seals to legal persons, so the reference must be resolvable.
Scheme syntax, registration and resolution commitments, as modelled by the DOI system under ISO 26324, are governed outside this model; only scheme, value and assigning authority are carried here.
Retention triggers and validity periods anchor to calendar and working-day rules held elsewhere; this model constrains stored values to RFC 3339 instants with explicit offsets.
Message attachments resolve to records governed here; eIDAS keeps electronic registered delivery services distinct from electronic documents, so transport semantics stay in the communication model.
PREMIS separates File and Bitstream objects from the intellectual entity; byte storage, replication and tiering are referenced, not modelled here.
Descriptive metadata facet applied to every record: title, creator, issued, modified, format, extent, language, accessRights, license, provenance and the version and replacement relations.

composition.target: ISO 15489-1:2016 Records management — Concepts and principles
composition.purpose: Vocabulary alignment for records, metadata for records, records systems, records processes and the characteristics of authoritative records; alignment only, no conformance claimed.

composition.target: PREMIS Data Dictionary for Preservation Metadata 3.0
composition.purpose: Alignment for object categories, fixity, format, significant properties, storage, and the Event, Agent and Rights entities used by the preservation and audit findings.
Alignment for the record resource versus instantiation split, documentary form and carrier types, and the partitive and provenance relations.
Alignment for derivation, generation, attribution, association and delegation, and for bundling provenance as an entity in its own right.
Alignment for electronic document, signature and seal tiers, electronic time stamps and validation; the tier vocabulary is EU-specific and other jurisdictions map differently.

composition.target: UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Commerce (1996)
composition.purpose: Alignment for functional equivalence: the criteria under which an electronic instantiation satisfies paper concepts of writing, signature and original.
Alignment for asset-level provenance manifests, hard and soft bindings, ingredients and validation, used where content credentials travel with a rendition.
Normative value space for the mediaType element on instantiations and exchange packages.
Value space for fine-grained format identifiers and rendering dependencies beyond what media types express.

composition.target: NARA Universal ERM Requirements v3 and MoReq2010 v1.1
composition.purpose: Alignment for the operating surface: capture, maintenance and use, disposal, transfer, metadata and reporting, plus disposal scheduling and disposal holding as separate services.

owner_package_requirements: Name one accountable record owner (the author or issuing organization) and, separately, any custodian; the package must state that custody never confers ownership and that a custodian cannot widen access or dispose.
Declare every retention authority instrument the Dimension operates under, with its jurisdiction, period of force and precedence rule when two instruments collide.
Publish the identifier schemes in use and the resolution endpoint for each before any record is registered, together with the non-reuse guarantee.
Declare the accepted fixity algorithms, the minimum signature assurance tier per documentary form, and the algorithm sunset dates that trigger evidence renewal.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a registry-rooted namespace such as vr.wm-rec-001 for model terms and a separate, resolvable namespace for instance identifiers. Never reuse an instance IRI for a different record, even after disposition; a disposed record keeps its IRI as a tombstone. Keep term IRIs stable across projections — JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are renderings of the same terms.
registry_links: IANA Media Types registry for every mediaType value (SRC-009)
PRONOM for fine-grained format identification and rendering dependencies (SRC-014)
DOI registration agencies under ISO 26324 where a citable persistent identifier is required (SRC-015)
The competent archival authority's approved records schedules for retention classes and disposition authority citations (SRC-011)

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is the ordered set of semantic fields, not any serialisation; storage and interface formats are projections and must round-trip the semantics.
Normalise every timestamp to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z before comparison or hashing; never normalise to local time.
Canonicalise identifiers as scheme plus value; comparison is case-sensitive unless the governing scheme declares otherwise.
Hash content and metadata under separate digests, so that a permitted metadata correction cannot invalidate a content fixity value.
patch_rules: Issued versions are immutable: a correction is a new version with a supersession link and a change note, never an in-place edit.

Descriptive and control metadata may be patched in place, but each patch writes an event entry carrying the previous value, the new value, the actor, the reason, the event time and the observation time.
A patch must never change identity, retention class, recorded fixity values or a signature binding; each of those requires the corresponding governed function.
Patches to a record under an active hold are rejected unless the hold instrument explicitly permits metadata correction, and the permission is cited in the event.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional field or a vocabulary term is a minor change; removing a field, tightening cardinality, or changing identifier granularity or semantics is breaking.
External alignments may be added, re-versioned or withdrawn without a breaking change, but a conformance claim may never be added without a cited evidence artifact.
Deprecated terms are retained with a deprecation date and a replacement pointer for at least one major version, and remain resolvable thereafter.

identity_priority: First: the authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record, such as a register entry number or an issuing organization's document number.
Second: a governed global identifier or IRI, such as a DOI under ISO 26324, a Handle, an ARK or a registry-governed IRI with a published persistence commitment.
Third: a UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, recorded together with the minting agent and the RFC 3339 minting instant.
Never an identifier: a date, a title, a file name, a storage path or a content digest. A digest is a fixity value and is identical across duplicate copies, so it cannot denote a record.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; where the offset is genuinely unknown use the -00:00 convention rather than assuming Z. Event time (when it happened) and observation or ingestion time (when the system learned of it) are always stored as separate fields and neither is inferred from the other.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts — versions, fixity manifests, format reports, validation reports, event entries, holds, receipts, disposition certificates and packages — are named <record-identifier>/<artifact-kind>/<zero-padded-sequence>-<RFC 3339 UTC instant>. Sequences are monotonic per record and per kind, and are never reused or renumbered, including after an artifact body is deleted.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries at least one fixity value with a named algorithm and its RFC 3339 computation instant. Artifacts with legal effect additionally carry a signature or seal and, where obtainable, a trusted time-stamp token so that their evidential value survives credential expiry or revocation. Integrity failures are recorded as events and recovered from a verified replica; they are never silently repaired.

policies: No conformance to ISO 15489, PREMIS, RiC, eIDAS, C2PA, MoReq2010 or NARA requirements may be published without a cited evidence artifact naming the validating party and date; external standards are otherwise carried as alignments only.

Disposition is irreversible and therefore requires an in-force authority instrument, an elapsed retention period, a hold check performed at the moment of execution, two-party authorisation, and a surviving evidence artifact plus tombstone.
Access to record content is granted by the owner; a custodian may narrow but never widen access, and every grant, denial, exception and emergency access is logged with the same fidelity.
Personal data within a record is processed only on a declared lawful basis; redaction produces a new derivative instantiation linked to its source and never overwrites the source.
The audit trail, hold instruments and disposition evidence are stored so that disposing of the record does not erase them.

read: Existence-level metadata — identifier, documentary form, classification, key dates, status — is readable by any authenticated agent unless the record carries a restriction that covers existence itself.
Reading content requires an access decision recorded against the requester, the stated purpose, the scope and the RFC 3339 decision instant.
Reads of records under an active hold are logged with the hold reference so that the reading is discoverable in proceedings.
create: Creation requires an identifier assigned by the identity priority, a documentary form, a classification class, a responsible agent and an event time.
Capture of an externally received record preserves the received bytes unaltered and records the receipt event before any normalisation, which is then recorded as a separate derivative.
update: Only descriptive and control metadata may be updated in place; any change to content requires a new version.
Every update writes an event entry with actor, reason, previous and new values, event time and observation time.
delete: Logical withdrawal from active use is a distinct state from physical destruction and must never be conflated with it.

Physical destruction executes only through the disposition function and always leaves a disposition certificate and a tombstone retaining identifier, form, classification, key dates and the authority applied.
Deletion of provenance, audit-trail, hold or disposition-evidence artifacts is prohibited while the parent record exists, and those artifacts outlive the record under their own schedule.

roles.name: Record owner (author or issuing organization)
responsibilities: Accountable for the record's existence, accuracy and classification
Grants and revokes access to content and metadata
Authorises issuance of new versions and approves disposition

roles.name: Custodian or registrar
responsibilities: Holds the record and maintains the register entry on the owner's behalf
Maintains fixity, storage and the chain of custody without acquiring ownership
Escalates to the owner any request that would widen access or alter content

roles.name: Records manager
responsibilities: Maintains the classification scheme and retention schedules and their authority citations
Resolves schedule conflicts under the declared precedence rule
Runs the disposition worklist and obtains the required authorisations

roles.name: Preservation engineer
responsibilities: Performs format identification, characterisation and fixity verification on schedule
Plans and executes migration or emulation before format obsolescence
Records every preservation action as an event with byte-change status

roles.name: Legal hold custodian
responsibilities: Places, scopes, monitors and releases holds under a named authority
Verifies that no automated process can dispose of an in-scope record
Retains hold instruments and release evidence independently of the records held

roles.name: Access and data protection officer
responsibilities: Applies security markings, statutory exemptions and restriction review dates
Decides access requests and approves redacted derivatives for release
Reviews break-glass events and notifies owners within the declared window

roles.name: Auditor
responsibilities: Reads holds, events, fixity artifacts and access logs without content access
Tests that the audit trail is append-only and that disposition evidence survives
Reports unexplained custody gaps and unverifiable conformance claims

access.default_rule: Deny by default for record content. Existence-level metadata is readable by authenticated agents unless the record carries a restriction that extends to its existence; every content read requires a recorded decision.
exceptions: Statutory access rights such as freedom-of-information and data-subject access override an owner's denial, subject to the declared exemptions and their review dates.
Legal hold custodians and auditors receive read access to holds, event history, fixity artifacts and access logs without any right to content.
Emergency break-glass access is available to named roles, is logged in full, and triggers notification to the owner within the declared window.
Receiving archives obtain full read access to transferred records and their evidence at the moment custody transfers, under the transfer instrument.
audit_requirements: Log requester identity, stated purpose, requested scope, decision, decision-maker and the RFC 3339 decision instant for every access event.
Retain access logs at least as long as the record's retention period and store them separately, so that disposition of the record does not erase the trail.
Log denied and failed access attempts at the same fidelity as grants, and review break-glass events on a declared cycle.
Record which projection was served, so that an omission can later be distinguished from an absence of data.

read_order: AGENTS.md — model name, type and the four resolvable URLs, plus owner, identifier scheme and default access rule
Specification URL — bundles, layers, findings, questions and data elements, and the boundaries to sibling models
Storage type URL — how the chosen projection stores records, versions, instantiations, events and artifacts, and what it cannot express
Interface URL — read, create, update and delete rules and the governed function endpoints
Processes URL — capture, versioning, signing, validation, custody transfer, hold, disposition and export workflows
